title: Part Grounding, Not Action Knowledge: Locating the Bottleneck in VLM Affordance Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2609.13225v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Benchmarks agree that vision-language models reason poorly about low-level manipulation, but an aggregate accuracy score does not say which step fails. We separate two steps that affordance questions conflate: identifying which part of an object to act on, and knowing what action that part requires. Across 19 articulated objects we asked eight models, spanning three developers, what motion a robot should apply. Under an open prompt, push was produced once in 64 evaluations where it was correct, despite being correct for 8 of 19 objects and appearing in the offered label set every time. Inspecting the outputs showed why: models described a different part than the one being scored, e.g. explaining how to pick up a camera rather than press its button. translated_title: 部件定位，而非动作知识：定位视觉-语言模型可供性预测的瓶颈
translated_abstract: 各基准测试一致表明，视觉-语言模型（VLM）在低层操作推理方面表现不佳，但总体准确率分数无法说明具体是哪一步失败了。我们将可供性问题中混淆的两个步骤分离开来：识别物体上应该操作哪个部件，以及知道该部件需要什么动作。在19个铰接物体上，我们询问了来自三个开发商的八个模型，机器人应该施加什么运动。在开放提示下，“推”这一动作在64次评估中仅在答案正确时被生成了一次，尽管它在19个物体中的8个上是正确答案，并且每次都出现在所提供的标签集中。对输出的检查揭示了原因：模型描述的是与被评分部件不同的部件，例如解释如何拿起相机而不是按下其按钮。明确命名目标部件使每个模型的动作准确率提升了0.32到0.63，从0.158-0.474提高到0.684-0.947，“推”的召回率从0-1/8提高到7-8/8。没有任何模型能够胜过一个恒定的、忽略问题的答案（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究发现VLM可供性预测的瓶颈在于部件定位而非动作知识——明确命名目标部件可使所有模型的动作准确率提升0.32至0.63，证明模型失败的原因是识别错了物体部件而非不知道该部件所需的动作。
en_tdlr: The bottleneck in VLM affordance prediction is part grounding rather than action knowledge—explicitly naming the target part boosts action accuracy by 0.32 to 0.63 across all models, showing models fail at identifying the correct object part rather than at knowing the required action.
